newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down, Central Bank intervenes.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed marginally lower on Tuesday at 26.289 to the dollar from 26.285 as the Central Bank kept buying dollars, dealers said.

Traders said the Central Bank purchased about $61 million to $84 million at 26.284, 26.286 and 26.287 after banks were swamped with dollars for portfolio and direct investments as well as overseas contract workers' remittances.
The day's average yielded a stronger peso at 26.287 versus 26.289, with turnover slightly lower at $200.80 million from $205.30 million.
"The Central Bank is there to support the dollar. It wants to build up its international reserves because of the widening trade deficit," a dealer said.
"Without the Central Bank, the rate would have been at 26.25 pesos," another said.
The peso could still gain in the coming days because of strong dollar inflows, traders said. But the Central Bank will keep the peso stable through its tight rein in the market, they said.
